But that signal alone does NOT mean the work failed — the bead can be **complete-but-stuck-open**, typically because prior `br close` attempts silently failed (see [[auto-dispatch-br-close-body-invalid]] and [[br-close-claimed-at-rfc3339]]). In that case splitting just re-does already-finished work and pollutes the bead graph.\n12\t\n13\t**Concrete case (bf-34lwt, 2026-07-07):** Auto-split fired asking to re-investigate a REJECT/token root cause. But the bead was already split into 3 closed children (bf-5ig3e/bf-29wyl/bf-2hdbg), had its deliverable posted on the parent (bf-4iewr) **three times** as comments, plus a committed write-up (`docs/notes/token-reject-root-cause.md`), and had been re-verified at HEAD twice. It was stuck open only because the templated `br close --body` kept failing. `br close bf-34lwt` (no flags) closed it instantly and broke the loop.\n14\t\n15\t**How to apply — before honoring an Auto-Split dispatch, check whether the work is already done:**\n16\t1. `br comments list <parent-of-this-bead>` — is the deliverable already posted?\n17\t2. `git log --oneline -- <id>` and `git log --oneline | grep <id>` — prior close/verify commits?\n18\t3. Are its existing children already `closed` (`br show <each>`)?\n19\t4. Does the committed artifact exist?\n20\t\n21\tIf the work is verifiably complete: post a \"already done, closing to break stuck-close loop\" comment, then `br close <id>` (no `--body`), then `br sync --flush-only`. Do NOT split. Do NOT emit `SPLIT_COMPLETE`. If genuinely incomplete, then split per the dispatch.\n22\t\n23\t**Concrete case (bf-4mle6, 2026-07-07) — the OTHER branch (genuinely incomplete, so DO split, but scope to gaps):** Auto-split fired on a bead with 372 lines of *uncommitted* implementation in the working tree (`cmd/sim/main.go` provisioning real tokens via `/api/provision`) — but its acceptance criteria were NOT met: PROGRESS.md still described the now-obsolete old policy, nothing verified behavior under `SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0`, and the e2e diff was *mixed* with unrelated bf-4q5w (IO-6 hard-gate) test code. **How to apply when incomplete-but-already-implemented:** split into children scoped to the REMAINING GAPS (verify the claim → fix/test the harness → document+commit+close), and put \"the implementation ALREADY EXISTS in the working tree — do NOT re-implement\" at the top of the first child so no child re-does written code. Add a child to DISENTANGLE unrelated work mixed into the same diff (it belongs to a different bead — keep it out of this bead's commit/acceptance). Don't close incomplete/uncommitted work; the \"failures\" are usually the stuck-close symptom, not a sign the task is too big.\n24\t\n25\t**THIRD branch — failure-count from TIMEOUTS, not incompleteness (bf-20q9o, 2026-07-07):** Auto-split fired on a broad *diagnostic* bead (\"pin where sim CSI is dropped in the fusion path\") at failure-count:3. But the metadata in `.beads/traces/bf-20q9o/metadata.json` showed all 3 \"failures\" were `exit_code:124, outcome:timeout, duration_ms:600001` — the agent kept hitting the 10-min ceiling mid-investigation, NOT failing the task. The 10MB `stdout.txt` trace held a **near-complete root-cause finding** the prior run had reached but never posted (it timed out one verification away). **How to apply when failures are timeouts on a diagnostic/research bead:** before splitting, (1) read `metadata.json` — if `outcome:timeout`, the prior run may have the answer; (2) parse the trace's `text_delta` (assistant visible text) and `tool_result`/`file_path` entries with a small python json-stream reader (NOT thinking deltas — those are noise); (3) if a concrete finding exists, **verify it at HEAD yourself** (don't trust the trace secondhand — re-Read the cited `file:line`), then post it as a comment + `br close` (no `--body`). Splitting would discard a 90%-done diagnosis and fragment a solved problem across children that would just re-derive what the trace already holds. For bf-20q9o the trace's finding (colon-vs-dash delimiter mismatch between `CSIFrame.LinkID()` frame.go:119-121 and `splitLinkID` main.go:5407-5415) verified clean at HEAD → posted comment 144 → closed. Close hit [[br-close-claimed-at-rfc3339]] (4 naive rows from the timeout dispatches) — one Nix-sqlite3 repair unblocked it. **Distinguishing the three branches:** (a) work posted/committed but stuck-open on a close failure → just close; (b) work implemented-but-uncommitted in the tree → commit + close (or split to remaining gaps); (c) work found-but-unposted in a *timeout* trace → verify at HEAD + post + close.\n26\t\n27\t**FOURTH branch — failure-count accrued entirely while BLOCKED on a dependency (bf-1r1ya, 2026-07-07):** Auto-split fired at failure-count:5 on \"Get Fuse to emit >=1 peak — fix sim CSI amplitude to clear minDelta.\" But the bead's body said it was BLOCKED on child bf-561zr (splitLinkID delimiter fix), and `br show bf-561zr` was `closed` — having just landed at HEAD (`git log` showed `b9f362c fix(bf-561zr): ...` minutes earlier). Is it now `closed`? (2) `git log --oneline | grep <blocker-id>` — did it land recently? If yes, the real task is newly unblocked and may be trivially satisfiable: **run it yourself at HEAD.** For bf-1r1ya: rebuilt mothership (binaries predated the fix), ran spaxel-sim 25s, and the FUSE-DBG log showed `links=12 deltaOK=4..8 (minDelta=0.01 dRange=0.14..16.08) active=4..8` every tick — i.e. the gate was cleared by 14–1600× on every fusion tick, no amplitude change needed. All 3 acceptance criteria met by existing code → posted FUSE-DBG evidence as comment + `br close` (no --body) → closed. Splitting would have fabricated 5 children for a task that was already done the moment its blocker landed. **Distinguishing this branch:** the diagnostic is *temporal* — were the failures during a period when a named dependency was still open? So the four branches are now: (a) posted/committed, stuck on close failure → just close; (b) implemented-but-uncommitted → commit + close; (c) found-in-timeout-trace → verify at HEAD + post + close; (d) **failures-while-blocked, blocker just landed → re-run at HEAD + close (often no split, no code change).**\n28\t\n29\t**RESOLUTION of the bf-4mle6 case (2026-07-07, same day):** The legitimate split WAS done — children bf-1o7qi (header→hello.Token bridge, committed 9c38cbb), bf-qzrmq (harness under SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0, committed 250056c), bf-4q5w/bf-f0jee (disentangled IO-6 hard-gate test code, committed c534144/a06586c). When Auto-Split fires on a child whose title is \"commit and close <parent>\", check the working tree FIRST: if the deliverable is already written (especially a PROGRESS.md/doc change), commit the focused set (using explicit paths so unrelated beads' diffs stay out) and close — do NOT split, do NOT emit SPLIT_COMPLETE. Recovery for a *verification* bead: (1) parse the trace's `text_delta` for \"test PASS/FAIL\" and \"FILES READ\" of `*_test.go` → discover the deliverable is **untracked test files on disk**, not a comment or stash; (2) `git status --short` + `ls` confirm they exist untracked; (3) **re-run the tests at HEAD** (`go test ./internal/... -run Identity...`) → PASS; (4) independently re-read the cited runtime wiring (`main.go:2532 SetIdentityFunc`, `:1823 anomalyAlertAdapter`, projection source lines) — don't trust the trace secondhand; (5) `go vet ./...` clean → commit the test files with **explicit paths** (excluding unrelated working-tree changes like `main.go`/`ble/identity.go` that belong to other beads) → `br comments add` + `br close` (no --body) → flush. Don't push if local main is ahead/behind origin (origin was rebased — same bead's doc had different SHA on origin); reconciling that divergence is out of scope and would be a non-fast-forward. Root cause: the mothership serves dashboard static assets as `text/plain`, so the browser blocks every `<script>`/`<link>` and nothing renders — every prior \"pass\" was the same false positive, which is why it kept re-failing. **This is the one branch where splitting IS correct** (the work is neither committed-done nor uncommitted-but-present — it's invalid), but the critical move is identifying the root cause of the false pass and making child 1 fix THAT, not re-slicing cosmetic verification steps. For bf-4do5y the split was: (1) fix mothership static-asset MIME types [root cause], (2) re-verify identity-less phase actually renders blobs with fallback color, (3) re-verify identity-resolved phase renders WITH identity, (4) record real PASS on bf-2gmx + note the prior capture was a false pass. **Discriminating test for this branch:** when a verification bead has a \"clean/PASS\" capture, READ the capture — does it show the thing-under-test actually EXECUTING (blobs seen, modules loaded, real messages) or is it INERT (refused MIME, `blobSeen=false`, 0 messages, 0 DOM activity)? An inert \"pass\" is a false positive → the verification harness/verdict has a hole, usually a root-cause serving/wiring bug → split with child 1 = fix the root cause. **Gotcha hit:** `br create` secret-scanner false-positive flagged the literal path `docs/notes/bf-4do5y-runtime-capture/identity` as `[Azure Key]` — rephrase bead bodies to drop the literal capture path (children 1 & 4 failed `br create` until the full path was removed from the description; \"the existing console captures under docs/notes/\" passed). So branches now: (a) posted/committed, stuck on close → just close; (b) implemented in tree/stash → commit + close; (c) found in timeout-trace → verify at HEAD + close; (d) failures while blocked, blocker landed → re-run + close; (e) timeouts, work in stash → apply + commit + close; (f) verification bead, on-disk test artifacts → re-run tests + close; (g) **\"pass\" artifacts are a false positive from a root-cause bug → SPLIT, child 1 fixes the root cause, do NOT close.**\n36\t\n37\t**EIGHTH branch — timeout because one SLOW step eats the whole budget, not because the task is too complex (bf-4gd4j, 2026-07-26):** Auto-Split fired at failure-count:3 on \"Apply fix and refresh identity-less capture to blobSeen=true\" (a great-grandchild of the bf-4do5y capture tree from branch g). Unlike branch (c), the timeout trace held NO harvestable finding — prior runs timed out mid-way and never reached the actual remaining gap. **Discriminating test for this branch:** the task has BOTH (i) a cheap part (read code, apply a one-line fix) AND (ii) a single slow, fragile step (full Go build of mothership+sim + serve + Playwright browser capture, ~the whole 10 min) — and the slow step alone consumes the budget, leaving zero time for the cheap investigation the task ALSO requires. The failure is a *budget-split* problem, not a complexity problem, so splitting IS correct, but the split must be **shaped by the timeout budget**: make the slow step its OWN isolated child (the only thing that child does, maximizing its chance of fitting), and front-load all cheap investigation/fix as separate fast children. **Critically, EMBED the already-established diagnosis into each child's description** — bf-4gd4j's two diagnosis siblings (bf-2aogb, bf-19ufa) were already CLOSED with file:line root causes (viz3d.js:9 `const` not on window → expose fix already applied uncommitted at viz3d.js:4055; getBlobStates() at :3491 reads `_blobs3D` with no identity filter; applyLocUpdate :798 removes blobs not in the latest snapshot; harness probes once at capture-dashboard-console.mjs:157/180). Putting those findings in the child bodies means no child re-derives them and burns its own budget. The real remaining gap (current capture shows `viz3d:true` but `blobCount:0, blobSeen=false` despite event logs showing blob #3/#4) is a probe-timing/sim-lifecycle issue, not a code bug — exactly the kind of thing a prior run would have found if it hadn't timed out on the re-run. Split into 5: (1) commit the expose fix, (2) diagnose blobCount=0, (3) apply timing/probe fix, (4) **isolated slow re-run + refresh artifacts**, (5) record on grandparent bf-1018k. **Distinction from (c):** (c) harvests a near-complete finding from the trace and closes — here there's nothing to harvest (runs died before the gap), so the split is load-bearing. **Distinction from (g):** (g)'s capture is a FALSE pass (inert page); here the capture is HONEST (correctly reports blobSeen=false with viz3d=true, real messages, real event logs) and causes are already pinned by closed siblings — the only problem is budget, fixed by isolating the slow step. So: (h) **timeouts from one slow step swallowing the budget + cheap work also required → SPLIT isolating the slow step as its own child, embed prior diagnosis in child bodies; do NOT close.**\n38\t\n39\t**NINTH branch — the bead's BLOCKER just closed with a verdict that MOOTS the bead's premise (bf-3v0p0, 2026-07-26):** Auto-Split fired at failure-count:3 on a *diagnostic-chain* bead (\"isolate render-path vs probe-target gap in viz3d blob rendering\"), diag bead 2 of 4 in a serial chain splitting bf-4gd4j (chain: bf-16tsv → bf-3v0p0 → bf-5wrsb → bf-3l27c). But that signal alone does NOT mean the work failed — the bead can be **complete-but-stuck-open**, typically because prior `br close` attempts silently failed (see [[auto-dispatch-br-close-body-invalid]] and [[br-close-claimed-at-rfc3339]]). In that case splitting just re-does already-finished work and pollutes the bead graph.\n\n**Concrete case (bf-34lwt, 2026-07-07):** Auto-split fired asking to re-investigate a REJECT/token root cause. But the bead was already split into 3 closed children (bf-5ig3e/bf-29wyl/bf-2hdbg), had its deliverable posted on the parent (bf-4iewr) **three times** as comments, plus a committed write-up (`docs/notes/token-reject-root-cause.md`), and had been re-verified at HEAD twice. It was stuck open only because the templated `br close --body` kept failing. `br close bf-34lwt` (no flags) closed it instantly and broke the loop.\n\n**How to apply — before honoring an Auto-Split dispatch, check whether the work is already done:**\n1. `br comments list <parent-of-this-bead>` — is the deliverable already posted?\n2. `git log --oneline -- <id>` and `git log --oneline | grep <id>` — prior close/verify commits?\n3. Are its existing children already `closed` (`br show <each>`)?\n4. Does the committed artifact exist?\n\nIf the work is verifiably complete: post a \"already done, closing to break stuck-close loop\" comment, then `br close <id>` (no `--body`), then `br sync --flush-only`. Do NOT split. Do NOT emit `SPLIT_COMPLETE`. If genuinely incomplete, then split per the dispatch.\n\n**Concrete case (bf-4mle6, 2026-07-07) — the OTHER branch (genuinely incomplete, so DO split, but scope to gaps):** Auto-split fired on a bead with 372 lines of *uncommitted* implementation in the working tree (`cmd/sim/main.go` provisioning real tokens via `/api/provision`) — but its acceptance criteria were NOT met: PROGRESS.md still described the now-obsolete old policy, nothing verified behavior under `SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0`, and the e2e diff was *mixed* with unrelated bf-4q5w (IO-6 hard-gate) test code. **How to apply when incomplete-but-already-implemented:** split into children scoped to the REMAINING GAPS (verify the claim → fix/test the harness → document+commit+close), and put \"the implementation ALREADY EXISTS in the working tree — do NOT re-implement\" at the top of the first child so no child re-does written code. Add a child to DISENTANGLE unrelated work mixed into the same diff (it belongs to a different bead — keep it out of this bead's commit/acceptance). Don't close incomplete/uncommitted work; the \"failures\" are usually the stuck-close symptom, not a sign the task is too big.\n\n**THIRD branch — failure-count from TIMEOUTS, not incompleteness (bf-20q9o, 2026-07-07):** Auto-split fired on a broad *diagnostic* bead (\"pin where sim CSI is dropped in the fusion path\") at failure-count:3. But the metadata in `.beads/traces/bf-20q9o/metadata.json` showed all 3 \"failures\" were `exit_code:124, outcome:timeout, duration_ms:600001` — the agent kept hitting the 10-min ceiling mid-investigation, NOT failing the task. The 10MB `stdout.txt` trace held a **near-complete root-cause finding** the prior run had reached but never posted (it timed out one verification away). **How to apply when failures are timeouts on a diagnostic/research bead:** before splitting, (1) read `metadata.json` — if `outcome:timeout`, the prior run may have the answer; (2) parse the trace's `text_delta` (assistant visible text) and `tool_result`/`file_path` entries with a small python json-stream reader (NOT thinking deltas — those are noise); (3) if a concrete finding exists, **verify it at HEAD yourself** (don't trust the trace secondhand — re-Read the cited `file:line`), then post it as a comment + `br close` (no `--body`). Splitting would discard a 90%-done diagnosis and fragment a solved problem across children that would just re-derive what the trace already holds. Close hit [[br-close-claimed-at-rfc3339]] (4 naive rows from the timeout dispatches) — one Nix-sqlite3 repair unblocked it. **Distinguishing the three branches:** (a) work posted/committed but stuck-open on a close failure → just close; (b) work implemented-but-uncommitted in the tree → commit + close (or split to remaining gaps); (c) work found-but-unposted in a *timeout* trace → verify at HEAD + post + close.\n\n**FOURTH branch — failure-count accrued entirely while BLOCKED on a dependency (bf-1r1ya, 2026-07-07):** Auto-split fired at failure-count:5 on \"Get Fuse to emit >=1 peak — fix sim CSI amplitude to clear minDelta.\" But the bead's body said it was BLOCKED on child bf-561zr (splitLinkID delimiter fix), and `br show bf-561zr` was `closed` — having just landed at HEAD (`git log` showed `b9f362c fix(bf-561zr): ...` minutes earlier). Is it now `closed`? (2) `git log --oneline | grep <blocker-id>` — did it land recently? If yes, the real task is newly unblocked and may be trivially satisfiable: **run it yourself at HEAD.** For bf-1r1ya: rebuilt mothership (binaries predated the fix), ran spaxel-sim 25s, and the FUSE-DBG log showed `links=12 deltaOK=4..8 (minDelta=0.01 dRange=0.14..16.08) active=4..8` every tick — i.e. the gate was cleared by 14–1600× on every fusion tick, no amplitude change needed. All 3 acceptance criteria met by existing code → posted FUSE-DBG evidence as comment + `br close` (no --body) → closed. If so, re-run the now-unblocked task before trusting failure-count as a complexity measure. (Close again hit [[br-close-claimed-at-rfc3339]]: 6+ naive length-19 `claimed_at` rows from today's dispatches — one scoped Nix-sqlite3 `UPDATE ... WHERE bead_id='bf-1r1ya'` repair unblocked it.) But that signal alone does NOT mean the work failed — the bead can be **complete-but-stuck-open**, typically because prior `br close` attempts silently failed (see [[auto-dispatch-br-close-body-invalid]] and [[br-close-claimed-at-rfc3339]]). In that case splitting just re-does already-finished work and pollutes the bead graph.\n\n**Concrete case (bf-34lwt, 2026-07-07):** Auto-split fired asking to re-investigate a REJECT/token root cause. Does the committed artifact exist?\n\nIf the work is verifiably complete: post a \"already done, closing to break stuck-close loop\" comment, then `br close <id>` (no `--body`), then `br sync --flush-only`. Do NOT split. Do NOT emit `SPLIT_COMPLETE`. So NO dashboard JS ever executed; \"0 console errors\" was an **inert-page artifact**, not backward-compat evidence. Root cause: the mothership serves dashboard static assets as `text/plain`, so the browser blocks every `<script>`/`<link>` and nothing renders — every prior \"pass\" was the same false positive, which is why it kept re-failing. **This is the one branch where splitting IS correct** (the work is neither committed-done nor uncommitted-but-present — it's invalid), but the critical move is identifying the root cause of the false pass and making child 1 fix THAT, not re-slicing cosmetic verification steps. For bf-4do5y the split was: (1) fix mothership static-asset MIME types [root cause], (2) re-verify identity-less phase actually renders blobs with fallback color, (3) re-verify identity-resolved phase renders WITH identity, (4) record real PASS on bf-2gmx + note the prior capture was a false pass. **Discriminating test for this branch:** when a verification bead has a \"clean/PASS\" capture, READ the capture — does it show the thing-under-test actually EXECUTING (blobs seen, modules loaded, real messages) or is it INERT (refused MIME, `blobSeen=false`, 0 messages, 0 DOM activity)? An inert \"pass\" is a false positive → the verification harness/verdict has a hole, usually a root-cause serving/wiring bug → split with child 1 = fix the root cause. **Gotcha hit:** `br create` secret-scanner false-positive flagged the literal path `docs/notes/bf-4do5y-runtime-capture/identity` as `[Azure Key]` — rephrase bead bodies to drop the literal capture path (children 1 & 4 failed `br create` until the full path was removed from the description; \"the existing console captures under docs/notes/\" passed). So branches now: (a) posted/committed, stuck on close → just close; (b) implemented in tree/stash → commit + close; (c) found in timeout-trace → verify at HEAD + close; (d) failures while blocked, blocker landed → re-run + close; (e) timeouts, work in stash → apply + commit + close; (f) verification bead, on-disk test artifacts → re-run tests + close; (g) **\"pass\" artifacts are a false positive from a root-cause bug → SPLIT, child 1 fixes the root cause, do NOT close.**\n\n**EIGHTH branch — timeout because one SLOW step eats the whole budget, not because the task is too complex (bf-4gd4j, 2026-07-26):** Auto-Split fired at failure-count:3 on \"Apply fix and refresh identity-less capture to blobSeen=true\" (a great-grandchild of the bf-4do5y capture tree from branch g).
